figures.finding: Curaçao levies its own income tax (Landsverordening op de inkomstenbelasting 1943): for 2026, 9.75% to XCG 39,094, then 15%, 23%, 30%, 37.5% and 46.5% above XCG 162,894, less a basic credit (basiskorting) of XCG 2,915.
figures.applies: From 1 January 2026; amounts indexed each year by ministerial regulation (art. 25 of the ordinance). Cg is the Caribbean guilder (XCG).

sources.said: De basiskorting, bedoeld in het tweede lid, wordt vastgesteld op: Cg 2.915,-.
Deze regeling treedt in werking met ingang van 1 januari 2026.

figures.finding: An employee pays 6% (employer 9%) for old-age insurance AOV and 0.5% each for AWW, on income up to XCG 100,000 (1% for the employee above); basic health insurance BVZ is 4.3% employee and 9.3% employer to XCG 150,000, with 13.6% for the self-employed; AVBZ 1.5% employee and 0.5% employer; ZV 1.9% and OV 0.5–5% fall on the employer.
figures.applies: 2026. The self-employed share of AOV/AWW was not stated in the table.

figures.finding: The employer withholds wage tax from pay by daily, weekly or monthly tables.

sources.said: An employer must withhold wage tax, which is based on daily, weekly, or monthly tables.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed only on Curaçao-source income, at the same progressive rates; there is no withholding on royalties or on fees for technical services.

sources.said: Nonresidents are taxed only on Curaçao-source income.
There is no withholding tax on royalties.
There is no withholding tax on fees for technical services.

figures.finding: Curaçao levies a turnover tax (omzetbelasting) of 6% standard, 7% or 9% in some cases, on goods and services; every supplier must in principle register, with no threshold given.

sources.said: The standard rate is 6%, with 7% and 9% rates applicable in certain cases.
Residents and nonresidents that carry out taxable supplies of goods or services in Curaçao must, in principle, register for sales tax.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; where tax is due the return is filed within six months of its end.
figures.applies: Due date read as six months after 31 December.

sources.said: The tax year is the calendar year.
If tax is due, the taxpayer must file a tax return within six months after the end of the tax year.
